subject: Re: Warm trial — quick qualifying questions before we lock a demo
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@parcelly.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: Kathy Li <kathy@parcelly.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interested in a short demo — trial live

Hi Olga,

We spun up a self-serve trial this week and I landed some simple POC traffic against the hosted API. The team liked the latency and the embeddings capabilities. Before we book a demo with your engineering team, a couple quick context items so the meeting is productive: 

- Use case: search + contextual answers inside our customer support portal (hybrid retrieval + generation).
- Expected volume: starting ~120qps at peak, mostly short queries (avg tokens/request ~40) but occasional long-read summarization jobs.
- Timeline: pilot to start in July; production rollout planned for Q4 if the pilot looks good.

Attaching a small traffic snapshot and a sample prompt set. Can Ben (SDR) help with calendar options?

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Senior PM, Parcelly

attachment: sample_prompt_set.txt (TXT, 6KB)

Hi Alex — great to hear the trial is already running. High level: sounds like a fit for our embeddings + hybrid retrieval flow. A couple clarifying Qs so we tailor the demo and make the most of the time: 

1) Are the 120 qps peak concurrent API calls or aggregate (burst) across multiple processes?
2) For the summarization jobs, do you expect them to be low concurrency but long context (6k+ tokens) or both long and concurrent?
3) Is data residency a requirement for the pilot (e.g., all inference in us-west)?

Ben, can you propose 3 slots (30m) for next week in PST that include an engineering attendee? I’ll bring a short playbook for prefix caching + batching and a couple model recommendations.

Best,
Olga
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Ben/Olga,

Thanks — quick clarifications:
- 120 qps is aggregated peak from our edge collector (will likely be served by a handful of worker processes; peak sustained for ~10–20 minutes during business hours).
- Summarization: we have two flavors: 1) short single-doc summarizations (~1.2k tokens) at modest concurrency, and 2) nightly batch jobs that summarize long threads (~8k tokens) but those are non-latency-critical.
- Data residency: must be in us-west for the pilot due to internal compliance.

All proposed slots look fine except Wed 1 Jul 14:00 (we have an internal planning meeting). Could we do Tue 30 Jun 10:00 PT? If so, please send a calendar invite and any pre-read.
